historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 11, Page 237-242. The name Munqiz carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Munqiz bin Ar-Rabiah Al-Ansari was the leader of the Arab tribes of Kheybar after the death of Muhammad (pbuh). He refused to pay the Zakat (Charitable Tax) to the Caliph Umar bin Al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him). This led to a military campaign against him. Munqiz was killed in battle and the people of Kheybar agreed to pay their Zakat to the Caliph.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Hisham's Sirat Ibn Hisham, Volume 2, Page 478-479. The name Munqiz carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Munqiz bin Ar-Rabiah Al-Ansari was a leader of the Arab tribes of Kheybar before the advent of Islam. He was responsible for the killing of Ka'ab bin Al-Ashraf, a poet and enemy of the early Muslims. This act led to the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his companions to launch a military campaign against the people of Kheybar. Munqiz was killed in battle and the people of Kheybar agreed to accept Islam.
